bugs.error_message: User asked for 'an easier possibility to update or insert data in the cloudkit data model' -- updates to existing CloudKit records were unreliable/silent-failing
bugs.root_cause: Every push* function builds a brand-new CKRecord(recordType:recordID:) instance rather than fetching the existing server record first, so it never carries a recordChangeTag. The shared save() helper called CKDatabase.save(_:), whose default save policy (.ifServerRecordUnchanged) treats a record with no change tag as an unverifiable conflict against any existing server record with the same recordID -- so CKError.serverRecordChanged is thrown on the second and every subsequent push of the same id (i.e. inserts worked, updates silently failed). The error was only printed to the console (print(...) inside a Task's catch), never surfaced, so it looked like intermittent/silent update failures rather than a clear crash.
bugs.fix: Replaced the single-record CKDatabase.save(_:) call in the private save(_:) helper (and the separate inline save in pushEventImage) with a CKModifyRecordsOperation configured with savePolicy = .changedKeys, wrapped in withCheckedThrowingContinuation for async/await use (new private upsert(_:) method). .changedKeys always writes the fields present on the record regardless of whether a server copy exists or what its change tag is, making every push* function a true insert-or-update with no conflict handling needed.

bugs.error_message: User-reported: 'When i open the one training in the Trainings view, the app crashed.' — real crash confirmed via devicectl crash log (EXC_BREAKPOINT/SIGTRAP, fatal SwiftData assertion) inside TeamMembership.id.getter, called from TrainingDetailView.attendance(for:)'s `training.attendances.first { $0.membership.id == membership.id }`.
bugs.root_cause: Attendance.membership: TeamMembership is a non-optional to-one relationship with no explicit @Relationship deleteRule/inverse declared on the TeamMembership side. TeamsViews' roster swipe-to-delete (and Team's own cascade delete of its memberships) called modelContext.delete(membership) directly. SwiftData's default deleteRule for an undeclared to-one relationship is .nullify, which cannot null a non-optional Swift property — this corrupts the dependent Attendance's local backing row instead of failing cleanly. Any later access to that Attendance's membership.id (TrainingDetailView/TournamentDetailView.attendance(for:)) then crashes with a fatal SwiftData assertion (_assertionFailure inside the @Model-macro-generated id getter).
